edit.description: the fanout cherry-pick loop's pre-check and commitPendingUpdate's pre-check switch from tip-sha-equality to a live-foreign-claim check (reuse git.ts tipClaimPath/liveTipClaimPid): no live foreign claim absorbs (cherry-pick onto whatever tip is current, abort-into-MergeFailure on conflict); a live foreign claim still refuses. Add headSha to TickVerdictMergeOutcome, populated at every merge-outcome push site.
operator commit mid-wave absorbs instead of refusing tipMoved; a live foreign engine claim still refuses; verdict merge outcomes carry headSha.

summary: Merge sites arbitrate on a live tip claim, not sha equality — a clean foreign commit absorbs, a conflicting one aborts into MergeFailure; verdict records each span's head sha.

per.section: Tip verify — one writer per branch, absorption at the merge

tests: a wave's cherry-pick loop absorbs a foreign non-engine commit landing mid-wave instead of refusing tipMoved
a live foreign tip claim still refuses the cherry-pick and the ledger commit
commitPendingUpdate recommits on whatever tip is current when no foreign claim holds it
a TickVerdictMergeOutcome carries the merged span's head sha
acceptance: No sha-equality check remains at a merge site; every merge/ledger-commit site checks only for a live foreign claim; every mergeOutcome entry in the verdict carries headSha.
notes: Field-paid incidents 10/11: a six-wide wave voided by a file-disjoint operator commit whose gates had already passed; hours later the same check refused four builds over the dispatcher's own just-landed commit.

edit.description: add a reset --keep primitive for the primary-checkout revert path, refusing loudly on a textual collision instead of discarding either side.
the afterMerge gate-revert on the primary checkout (today git.hardResetTo(repoRoot, preCherry)) uses the new keep-semantics primitive; ephemeral-worktree reverts keep --hard.
reset --keep preserves an unrelated uncommitted change; a textual collision refuses loudly, both writers' work left intact.
an afterMerge revert on the trunk survives a bystander's staged or unstaged edit.

summary: Primary-checkout engine reverts use reset --keep and refuse loudly on textual collision, instead of --hard wiping bystander uncommitted state.

per.section: Tip verify — one writer per branch, absorption at the merge

tests: an afterMerge revert on the trunk leaves an operator's unrelated staged/unstaged edit intact
a revert whose diff textually collides with uncommitted trunk state refuses loudly instead of discarding either side
acceptance: No --hard reset touches the primary checkout; every primary-checkout revert is --keep with a loud refusal on collision. Ephemeral-worktree reverts are unaffected.
notes: Field-paid incident 8: a wave-merge reset destroyed staged operator content and a refused tick's unstaged writes together, recoverable only from an operator-side snapshot.

edit.description: readPending() and commitPendingUpdate's rewrite read resolve pending.json content via a committed-tip read instead of fs.readFile; readPendingTolerant stays disk-based (the declared exception).
add a helper that reads a path's content at a given ref (git show <ref>:<path>) for readPending to call.
a decide-read reflects the committed tip, ignoring an uncommitted working-tree edit to pending.json.

summary: Dispatcher's strict pending.json reads (decide-reads, ledger rewrite read) resolve from the committed HEAD tip, never the working tree.

per.section: Dispatch reads come from the tip, not the tree

tests: readPending() reads pending.json from the committed tip, ignoring an uncommitted working-tree edit to the same file
PendingParseFailure still throws when the tip's committed content fails to parse
acceptance: Every strict readPending() call resolves from HEAD, not disk; readPendingTolerant remains the sole disk-reading exception.
notes: Field-paid: a pickability read lagging a just-merged cherry-pick redispatched — and re-bailed, at full agent price — an already-shipped entry.

edit.description: thread createWorktree's base ref through to the wave-end harvestFriction call; harvestFriction filters the mirror dir to files new relative to that base (untracked, or absent from the base tree at that path) instead of moving every file found.
a friction note committed by a prior worktree and inherited by a later sibling's checkout is not re-harvested by that sibling.

summary: Friction harvest moves only files new relative to the worktree's base commit, so a committed note stops being re-relayed by every later worktree.
tests: a friction file untracked in the worktree is harvested
a friction-channel file already present at the worktree's base commit is left in place, not re-copied with a new tag prefix
acceptance: harvestFriction moves only base-delta-new files; a file the checkout itself brought in from a committed base is never re-harvested.
notes: Field-paid: one committed note became eight stamped copies across two waves before an operator intervened.

edit.description: new startup-sweep function: under the tip claim, remove every directory under the worktree base via the removeWorktree+win32-fallback path, then git worktree prune, then every branch under this instance's flume/[ns/]… grammar; warn loudly (never abort) on a surviving path, reported once at run level.
call the sweep once in the loop command's startup, after the tip claim is acquired and before the first tick — job run reuses this path already.

a worktree/branch abandoned by a killed fanout tick, whose entry is no longer in pending.json, is removed at the next loop start; empty base sweeps silently; a stuck removal warns once and does not abort.

summary: flume loop sweeps abandoned worktrees and flume/** branches at start, under the tip claim, closing the gap where a dropped entry leaked its worktree indefinitely.

per.section: Startup sweep — a dead wave's residue is removed at the next start

tests: a worktree/branch abandoned by a killed tick, whose entry is no longer pending, is removed at the next loop start
an empty worktree base sweeps silently
a directory that cannot be removed (EBUSY) warns once at run level and does not abort the run
acceptance: flume loop (and job run, via the shared loop path) removes every stale directory under the worktree base and every flume/[ns/]… branch belonging to this instance before the first tick.
notes: Per-wave stale-slug removal (createWorktree) only ever covered entries being re-provisioned; this closes the remaining gap named in spec/loop.md, Crash equals stop.

edit.description: add stop to SUBCOMMANDS/HELP_TOP; handler writes <flumeDir>/stop idempotently and prints the consequence; flume status gains a stop-flag line between supervisor liveness and tip claim; flume loop (and job run) refuses at start, exit 1 naming the path, when the flag is already present.

superviseLoop checks the stop flag at the same per-iteration boundary it re-reads the baton (never mid-tick); on seeing it, ends the run after the in-flight tick finishes and releases the claim/lock; SuperviseResult records why iteration ended for the completion summary, without changing loopExitCode's totals-based formula.
flume stop is idempotent and prints the consequence; flume status reports the flag; flume loop refuses at start with the flag present.
a stop flag written mid-run lets the in-flight tick finish, then ends the run and releases the claim/lock.

summary: flume stop writes <flumeDir>/stop; the supervisor finishes its in-flight tick then ends the run; a present flag refuses a fresh loop/job run start until removed.
tests: flume stop is idempotent — repeat call prints the same statement, exit 0
flume loop refuses to start with the flag already present, naming the path, exit 1
a stop flag written between tick children ends the run after the current tick finishes, without killing it
flume tick ignores the flag and runs normally
a stopped run's exit code still reflects run totals (errored/shipped), not a special stop code
acceptance: flume stop/status/loop behave per spec: idempotent write, checked only at the baton-reread boundary, refuse-at-start, no kill, no unstop verb, exit code unchanged by the stop path itself.
notes: Also spec/cli.md: Subcommand surface (stop verb) and 'flume status owes exactly this' (status line #3). Deliberately no unstop/resume verb — removing the flag is the operator's own ack.

edit.description: defaultTickRunner passes FLUME_TIP_CLAIM_HELD=<supervisor pid> in each spawned tick child's env.

flume tick: when FLUME_TIP_CLAIM_HELD is absent, acquire+release its own tip claim around the single tick, refusing exit 1 on a live foreign claim; when present, trust the supervisor's claim and take none itself.
a bare flume tick acquires and releases its own claim, refusing when another live process holds it.
a loop-spawned tick child does not re-acquire the claim its supervisor already holds.

summary: A bare flume tick now takes its own tip claim around the single tick; a loop-spawned child trusts the supervisor's claim via FLUME_TIP_CLAIM_HELD instead of probing pids.

per.section: The loop lock and the tip claim

tests: a bare flume tick with no other live claim-holder acquires and releases a claim around its single tick
a bare flume tick refuses exit 1 when a live process already holds the claim
a loop child spawned with FLUME_TIP_CLAIM_HELD set does not call acquireTipClaim itself
acceptance: Every tick — bare or loop-spawned — runs under exactly one live claim; a loop child never double-acquires, and a bare tick is no longer claimless.
notes: Closes the claimless-bare-tick gap: previously only loop-level ticks were guarded, leaving concurrent bare ticks to collide with only optimistic tip-verify between them.
